llm.summary: The skill’s Tencent Docs reporting purpose is real, but it has review-worthy risks around shared-report data exposure, unpinned runtime code execution, and credential/input handling.

dimensions.detail: Tencent Docs access and local memory files are proportionate to the reporting workflow, but broad shared-sheet reads, raw JSON construction from user-controlled fields, and command-line token handling exceed a clean least-privilege implementation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package declares mcporter as latest and repeatedly runs npx -y mcporter, including during setup and report operations, so reviewed behavior can change at runtime and execute newly resolved npm code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation discloses Tencent Docs read/write flows, but it overstates isolation by saying the skill only uses the user's authorized work data while the monthly read path can return any records visible in the shared sheet.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists user name, record_id, authorization state, and caches under the workspace memory directory, and stores the Tencent Docs token through mcporter home configuration; this is mostly disclosed but users should treat it as sensitive local state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core reporting, setup, project matching, Tencent Docs writes, and monthly summaries are purpose-aligned, but monthly reads query the shared daily-report sheet without using the configured user record ID, which conflicts with the stated user-scoped data access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only in an environment where all users are allowed to see the shared Tencent Docs report sheet, pin and vet mcporter before running it, avoid entering tokens directly on the command line, and treat the workspace memory and mcporter configuration as sensitive.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: After inspecting the full artifact, setup and project-matching scripts are supporting pieces of the declared daily-report workflow, not a separate hidden purpose.
[AE1] expected: The required SKILL.md and referenced artifact files were locally available and inspected for this adjudication.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-language interface is consistent with the skill's Chinese organizational daily-report use case and is not a security concern by itself.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading report data to Tencent Docs and storing local user configuration are expected for the stated purpose and are substantially disclosed in the documentation.
[RP1] unexpected: Runtime use of unpinned npx mcporter is not necessary for the reporting purpose and creates a material supply-chain and secret-exposure concern.
[SC1] unexpected: The package-level latest dependency reinforces the same unpinned dependency concern.
[T05] unexpected: The monthly read function accepts a user record ID but does not filter by it, so shared-sheet records for other people can be included in reads and summaries.
[T08] unexpected: The artifact repeatedly auto-downloads and executes mcporter at runtime instead of using a pinned, reviewed dependency.
[T09] unexpected: Report content, notes, record IDs, work type, and hours are interpolated directly into JSON API arguments without serialization or validation.
[T09] unexpected: The setup flow accepts the Tencent Docs token as a command-line argument and forwards it in child-process arguments, exposing it to shell history or process inspection risks.
